variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
set myName to "Alice"
set myAge to 30

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
set str to "Hello"
set num to 42
set isTrue to true
set myDate to current date
data_types.notes: Supports strings, integers, reals, booleans, dates, lists, and records.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
set sum to 5 + 3
if sum is equal to 8 and str begins with "H" then
	-- do something
end if

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
if val > 10 then
	log "Greater"
else if val = 10 then
	log "Equal"
else
	log "Lesser"
end if

for_loop.title: For Loop (Repeat)
for_loop.code:
repeat with i from 1 to 5
	log i
end repeat

set theList to {"apple", "banana"}
repeat with item in theList
	log item
end repeat
for_loop.notes: Use 'repeat with' for range and list iteration.

while_loop.title: While Loop (Repeat While)
while_loop.code:
set count to 1
repeat while count <= 5
	log count
	set count to count + 1
end repeat

functions.title: Handlers (Functions)
functions.code:
on greet(userName)
	return "Hello, " & userName
end greet

greet("Alice")

arrays.title: Lists (Arrays)
arrays.notes: Lists are 1-indexed. Items are accessed using 'item X of'.

maps.title: Records (Maps)
maps.code:
set colors to {apple:"red", banana:"yellow"}
set appleColor to apple of colors
maps.notes: Records are similar to maps/dictionaries. Keys must be valid identifiers or strings.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
try
	set x to 1 / 0
on error errMsg number errNum
	log "Error " & errNum & ": " & errMsg
end try
error_handling.notes: Use try/on error blocks. Can capture error message and number.

comments.title: Comments & Script Headers
comments.notes: AppleScript uses # for comments with script headers.

numbers.title: Numbers & Arithmetic
numbers.notes: AppleScript supports shell integer arithmetic and numeric expressions.

booleans.title: Booleans & Exit Codes
booleans.notes: AppleScript evaluates boolean status through exit codes (0 = success) and boolean primitives.

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Coercion
type_casting.code:
str_val="42"
# Arithmetic context forces integer coercion
num=$((str_val + 0))
type_casting.notes: AppleScript handles type conversion explicitly via type accelerators [type] or arithmetic evaluation.

strings.title: Strings & Quoting
strings.code:
single='Literal single quotes'
double="Expanded: ${USER}"
multiline="Line 1
Line 2"
strings.notes: AppleScript differentiates between single quotes (literal) and double quotes (variable expansion).

string_formatting.title: String Interpolation
string_formatting.notes: AppleScript provides in-string variable interpolation and printf formatting.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Case
pattern_matching.notes: AppleScript matches patterns with case statements or switch blocks with glob matching.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.code:
# Brace expansion
for i in {1..10..2}; do
    echo "$i"
done
range.notes: AppleScript constructs ranges with brace expansion {start..end} or range operators ..

iterators.title: Pipes & Iterators
iterators.code:
while IFS= read -r line; do
    echo "$line"
done < "file.txt"
iterators.notes: AppleScript streams data elements through command pipelines and loop iteration.

oop_classes.title: Classes / Structured Functions
oop_classes.notes: AppleScript defines reusable components through classes (PowerShell 5+) or modular functions.

lists.title: Arrays & Collections
lists.code:
items=("apple" "banana" "cherry")
items+=("date")
echo "${items[0]}" # apple
echo "${items[@]}" # all elements
lists.notes: AppleScript manages arrays using array lists @() or whitespace-delimited shell arrays.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: AppleScript emulates tuples through string delimiters, .NET Tuples, or positional variables.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Lists
sets.notes: AppleScript models unique sets using associative arrays or underlying runtime sets.

modules_import.title: Sourcing & Modules
modules_import.code:
# Source an external script
source ./utils.sh
# or: . ./utils.sh
modules_import.notes: AppleScript imports external functions using source (. in POSIX) or Import-Module.
